title: Reducedness is invariant under changing the scalar algebra by an algebra equivalence
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A$ be a commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], let $L$ and $M$ be fields equipped with $k$-algebra structures, and let $e:L\to M$ be a bijective $k$-algebra homomorphism. Then $A\otimes_k L$ is reduced if and only if $A\otimes_k M$ is reduced.

source.place: Tensor-product transport along an algebra equivalence, Tags 00CX and 05G3

proof.text: Choose the inverse function $d:M\to L$ of the bijection $e$. It is a $k$-algebra homomorphism in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]: applying the injective map $e$ to $d(m+m')$ and $d(m)+d(m')$ gives $m+m'$ in both cases, and the same argument proves preservation of multiplication, zero and one. For $r\in k$, both $d(\iota_M(r))$ and $\iota_L(r)$ map to $\iota_M(r)$, so $d$ commutes with the structure maps. Thus $de=1_L$ and $ed=1_M$ as algebra maps.

Put $S=A\otimes_kL$ and $T=A\otimes_kM$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives their commutative $k$-algebra structures, factor inclusions and multiplication $(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=aa'\otimes bb'$. In clause (2), take the target to be $T$ and the two maps to be $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $\ell\mapsto1\otimes e(\ell)$, the latter being the composite of $e$ and the right inclusion. This constructs a $k$-algebra map $F:S\to T$ with $F(a\otimes\ell)=(a\otimes1)(1\otimes e(\ell))=a\otimes e(\ell)$. Applying the same clause with target $S$ and maps $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, $m\mapsto1\otimes d(m)$ constructs a $k$-algebra map $G:T\to S$ satisfying $G(a\otimes m)=a\otimes d(m)$. All maps agree on $k$ because $e$ and $d$ do.

source.place: Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), proof: the universal property Hom(A tensor_R B,C)=Hom(A,C) x_Hom(R,C) Hom(B,C); algebra.tex Tags 00CX and 05G3

proof.text: For every pure tensor, $GF(a\otimes\ell)=a\otimes d(e(\ell))=a\otimes\ell$ and $FG(a\otimes m)=a\otimes e(d(m))=a\otimes m$. These maps are $k$-linear, and pure tensors generate the tensor product as a $k$-module by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Hence the displayed identities extend to every element: $GF=1_S$ and $FG=1_T$.

Assume $S$ is reduced, meaning that its only nilpotent element is zero (Stacks Tag 00B3). If $y\in T$ satisfies $y^n=0$ for some $n\ge1$, then $G(y)^n=G(y^n)=G(0)=0$. Preservation of powers follows by induction from preservation of multiplication and one. Reducedness of $S$ gives $G(y)=0$, and therefore $y=F(G(y))=F(0)=0$. Thus $T$ is reduced.

Conversely assume $T$ is reduced. If $x\in S$ satisfies $x^n=0$ for some $n\ge1$, then $F(x)^n=F(x^n)=0$, so $F(x)=0$ and $x=G(F(x))=G(0)=0$. Hence $S$ is reduced. Together with the preceding step this proves $A\otimes_kL$ reduced if and only if $A\otimes_kM$ reduced.
